searches.reason: Develop paired intervention probes that remove recent events, remove repeated preferences, or shuffle history order, then measure changes in top-ranked items. This can reveal whether SASRec relies on current intent, sustained preferences, or broad associations. Use training-history prefixes, matched random-removal controls, and per-dataset uncertainty estimates; treat perturbation sensitivity as evidence of model dependence rather than proof of user intent.
searches.query: sequential recommendation diagnostic probes history perturbation recent interaction ablation repeated preference order shuffling shortcut learning matched controls 2024 2025 2026

searches.reason: Connect qualitative feedback to observable recommendation failures using full-catalog unseen-item rankings and title/description evidence. Seek methods that distinguish supported complements, near-duplicate substitutes, and explicitly conflicting specifications while abstaining when ownership or compatibility is unknown. Validate evidence extraction on the twenty feedback users without inventing equipment needs, satisfaction, or latent traits.
searches.query: recommendation diagnosis complementary versus substitute products compatibility evidence title description selective prediction abstention user feedback full catalog ranking 2024 2025 2026

searches.reason: Replace uncalibrated training margins and embedding averages with diagnostics whose usefulness is tested across checkpoints and controlled model changes. Compare sampled-candidate and full-catalog behavior, normalize score-scale effects, report missing observations explicitly, and test whether probe changes predict category-level and macro validation HR@10 improvements within the search budget.
